author: haiku
label: pilot-junior-fix-01
changes: Step 1 and Step 5: the POST endpoint's two responses are now defined (200 text/csv vs 202 JSON), and the page-handling note moved from Step 5 into Step 1, because the page decides there (Q1).

Step 9: the claim now accepts a running row only when its attempt number is lower, and checks the rows-updated count. A zero-row claim returns without work. Without this, two runs of one attempt could both write (Q2, Q3).
Step 9 load: added a branch for a running row with the same attempt number, which returns. This closes the duplicate-delivery gap (Q3).

Step 10: defined the in-memory paging position and the end-of-data rule (stop when a page returns fewer than 5,000 rows). The earlier text did not say where the position is kept or when the loop ends (Q4).
Step 2 and Terms: defined the shape of filters and cols (query-string text parsed by the rows API), and that column names come from the report's column list and values are bound as parameters (Q5).
Step 4: the header row uses the names from cols. The earlier text said 'column labels' with no source, and the source is not in the files (Q5).
Step 8 and Step 14: stated where export_id comes from and why latest always matches the export on screen (Q6).

Step 15, Decision 5 and Open question 8: removed the timeout, exception and worker-death codes, because the queue does not document the error argument. All final failures store attempts_exhausted and the error text (Q7).

Decision 3, Step 11, Step 12 and Step 17: the file key changed from job_id to the attempt number, so it depends on nothing the queue does not document. The Step 12 update is conditioned on attempt and status, and the orphaned-file case is stated (Q8).
Step 11: a heartbeat that updates 0 rows now aborts the upload and stops. Before, a superseded run kept writing.
Step 16: corrected the rationale. The old text said the longest silence is the backoff, but a running attempt can be silent for up to its 30-minute limit, so the silence bound is about 35 minutes.
Step 6 and Step 7: a crash between the insert and the enqueue is now noted, and recovery by the stale guard is stated.
Step 13: noted that the email can be sent twice if recording email_sent_at fails, and that this is accepted.
Step 18: added a claim test (duplicate delivery produces one writer). Added negative numbers to the CSV round-trip check, since the formula guard affects them.
Open questions: added 8 (whether the queue passes the cause of failure) and 9 (the rows API parser's grammar, which is not in the files).

Step 10: added a 'Parse again' paragraph so the job re-runs the stored filters and cols text through the same parser and column check as Step 2, with the failure path stated (Q9 showed this was not defined).
Step 8: defined download_available as status done and before completed_at + 7 days, so the flag is no longer undefined (Q10).
Step 12: completed_at is now t0, taken just before complete_multipart, so the page's expiry is never later than the bucket's deletion (Q10 exposed the few-seconds mismatch).
Step 7: stated that enqueue is called once with no retry, and that a failed job_id save is logged while still returning 202 (Q11).

Step 17: corrected the 'two jobs only if an enqueue was retried' claim, which had no basis in the plan; duplicates come from queue redelivery, and a failed enqueue that still queued a job is covered by Step 9 (Q11).
Step 11: added the 0-row case for the upload_id save, which now aborts the just-started upload and returns (Q12).
Step 6: the stale guard now aborts upload_id, clears it in the same step, and repeats the staleness test in its condition so it cannot close a row that was just updated (Q13).
Step 16: cross-referenced the abort behaviour from Step 6 so the stale rule and its cleanup are stated together (Q13).
Step 18: added check 11 for the re-parse failure path (Q9).
Step 14: removed the duplicated expiry rule and pointed to Step 8, so there is one definition of expiry (Q10).
Open question 9: now names Steps 2 and 10 as relying on the parser (Q9).
Terms: added bucket, signed URL, and handler/ctx definitions so `exports`, `signed_url` and `ctx` are explained in the file (Q14, Q18).
Step 8: states what `latest` returns when the caller has no export (200 with null) and what the page shows then (Q15).
Step 9: names the handler and its registration, the two fields of ctx, and that Steps 9 to 13 run in one call under one timeout (Q18).
Step 13: defines `expires_at` as the link's own 24-hour expiry and tells the user in the email to reopen the report if the link has expired (Q17).
Step 14: the 410 decision is made from the row date before storage is called, and the 302 URL lifetime is capped at the time left before the 7-day date so it cannot outlive the object (Q16).
Step 18: added check 12 for the download expiry behaviour.
Open questions: added item 10 on how signature checks, expired links and early deletion are handled by storage (Q14, Q16, Q17).
holes: Q7: Step 15 says on final failure by worker death the error_code is attempts_exhausted. How does the handler know which of timeout, exception or worker death occurred from the `error` argument? (author: The queue's documentation does not say what the error argument contains, so the handler cannot tell timeout, exception and worker death apart. The plan no longer depends on it: every final failure gets error_code attempts_exhausted, with the text of error stored in error_message. Whether the queue supplies a cause is Open question 8.)
